major_events: In [第一章 小二上酒], Xu Fengnian returns to Northern Liang with his loyal servant Old Huang after a grueling three-year, 6000-mile journey, disguised as a beggar and refusing the marriage proposal with the Princess of Sui.
In [第二章 白狐儿脸] and [第五章 天下第一美人], Xu Fengnian recruits the mysterious swordsman Nangong Pushe (White Fox Face) to protect him, offering her access to Wulin manuals in Tingchao Pavilion.

In [第十二章 湖中有老魁] and [第十三章 带刀老魁，背匣老黄], Chu Kuangnu (Lake Old Kui) escapes from his underwater prison. Servant Old Huang steps in, revealing his martial arts as Sword Nine Huang and defeating the monster.
In [第十四章 劣马黄酒六千里], Old Huang leaves Northern Liang to travel to Wudi City (Martial Emperor City) to fight Wang Xianzhi and retrieve his lost sword.

In [第二十章 杀人赏雪], news arrives that Old Huang died at Wudi City after performing his ninth sword style ('剑九六千里') against Wang Xianzhi, leaving his sword box on the city wall, which prompts Xu Fengnian to learn martial arts.

In [第三十一章 大黄庭] and [第三十二章 一肩挑道], Wudang Sect's leader Wang Chonglou transfers his massive 'Da Huang Ting' internal energy to Xu Fengnian to forge an alliance between Wudang and Northern Liang before his passing.
In [第五十二章 白马出凉州], Xu Fengnian formally sets out on his second major journey out of Northern Liang, accompanied by a large carriage caravan, maids, and guards.

In [第五十七章 大雨小道立红甲] and [第五十八章 水珠对水甲], Xu Fengnian's caravan is ambushed in a heavy rain by the mysterious Earth and Water Talisman Red Armors (符将红甲). Li Chungang displays his combat power, and they defeat the threat.
In [第七十二章 青羊宫里杀神仙（上）] and [第七十四章 青羊宫里杀神仙（下）], Xu Fengnian's forces storm Qingyang Palace on Qingcheng Mountain to avenge their insults, defeating the guards and forcing Wu Lingsu to submit.

In [第八十二章 龙王爷一竿拦江] and [第八十五章 几笑一飞剑], when challenged by enemies on the river, the old sheepskin-coat swordsman Li Chungang uses a single bamboo pole to cross and intercept the river, showing his returned strength.

In [第九十三章 可敢一战] and [第九十四章 死战], Jingan King Zhao Heng coordinates a multi-expert ambush (including the Red Armor) at Xunyang River to assassinate Xu Fengnian. Li Chungang saves the caravan using his signature 'One Sleeve of Green Snake' technique.

In [第一百三十四章 曹官子] and [第一百三十六章 一袖如何两青蛇], Cao Changqing (Cao Guanzi), the remaining loyal scholar-general of Western Chu, arrives to take Jiang Ni away to rebuild Western Chu. Xu Fengnian allows her to go, gifting her his mother's legendary sword, Da Liang Longque.
In [第一百四十一章 马踏中门], Xu Fengnian rides his horse directly through the main gates of the Lu Family mansion in Jiangnan to confront and punish those who slandered his eldest sister, Xu Zhihu.

In [第一百六十三章 呵呵不呵呵] and [第一百六十四章 江湖飘总挨刀], the eccentric assassin girl (呵呵姑娘) attacks Xu Fengnian, explaining that she wants to kill him quickly to spare him from a slow, painful death in future conspiracies.

In [第一百八十一章 请老祖宗赴死] and [第一百八十二章 儒圣], Xuanyuan Jingcheng ascends to the Confucian Sage realm and challenges the degenerate ancestor Xuanyuan Dapan at Daxueping, summoning a massive lightning storm that kills them both.

In [第一百九十九章 仙人骑鹤下江南] and [第二百章 登仙？], Hong Xixiang on Wudang Mountain recovers his past-life memories of Lü Dongbin, breaks his vow never to descend the mountain, and rides a yellow crane down to Jiangnan to save Xu Zhihu.

In [第二百章 登仙？] and [第二百零一章 雷池和道理], Zhao Xuansu (disguised as the child '小虫子' / Little Insect) attempts to assassinate Xu Fengnian at Wudi City. Xu Fengnian, supported by Deng Tai'an's flying swords, slashes and destroys Zhao Xuansu's physical body.
character_state_transitions: Xu Fengnian: Transitions from a powerless, hidden playboy who refuses to learn martial arts to an active martial artist with Wudang's 'Da Huang Ting' internal energy and double blades in [第三十一章 大黄庭] and [第五十二章 白马出凉州].

Old Huang (Sword Nine Huang): Transitions from a cowardly, quiet horse groom and wine-stealing servant to a legendary sword master who fights to the death at Wudi City against Wang Xianzhi in [第十三章 带刀老魁，背匣老黄] and [第二十章 杀人赏雪].
Nangong Pushe: Transitions from a wandering swordsman seeking shelter to a resident researcher in Tingchao Pavilion, determined to study all manuals to defeat her enemies in [第二章 白狐儿脸] and [第六章 走一个].

Wang Chonglou: Transitions from the active, powerful leader of Wudang Sect to a dying elder who passes on his life-force and 'Da Huang Ting' energy to Xu Fengnian to secure Wudang's future, ending in his death in [第三十一章 大黄庭] and [第三十二章 一肩挑道].

Li Chungang: Transitions from a locked-away, one-armed old man in sheepskin coat under Tingchao Pavilion to a revived, sword-wielding mentor who regains his spirit and displays his unmatched sword skills like 'One Sleeve of Green Snake' in [第八十二章 龙王爷一竿拦江] and [第九十四章 死战].

Jiang Ni: Transitions from a bitter, revenge-seeking maid in the Northern Liang mansion to the recognized princess of Western Chu who leaves with Cao Changqing to restore her kingdom in [第一百三十四章 曹官子] and [第一百三十六章 一袖如何两青蛇].

Xuanyuan Jingcheng: Transitions from a weak, mocked scholar despised by his own wife and family to a supreme Confucian Sage (儒圣) who sacrifices his life to eradicate the family ancestor in [第一百八十一章 请老祖宗赴死] and [第一百八十二章 儒圣].

Hong Xixiang: Transitions from a timid, non-descending cow-riding Taoist on Wudang Mountain to a legendary reincarnation of Lü Dongbin who rides a yellow crane to Jiangnan to save his beloved in [第一百九十九章 仙人骑鹤下江南] and [第二百章 登仙？].

Zhao Xuansu: Transitions from a disguised child ('小虫子') traveling with Xu Fengnian's party to a powerful Longhu Mountain ancestor who reveals his true nature and has his physical body destroyed by Xu Fengnian's blade in [第二百章 登仙？] and [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].

Xuanyuan Qingfeng: Transitions from a proud, helpless daughter of Huishan caught in family conspiracies to the new master of the Huishan Xuanyuan family after the death of her father and ancestor in [第一百八十一章 请老祖宗赴死] and [第一百八十四章 还了个放屁].

Chu Kuangnu (Lake Old Kui): Transitions from an underwater prisoner trapped under the lake by chains to a freed martial artist who acts as a temporary protector/sparring partner for Xu Fengnian in [第十二章 湖中有老魁] and [第十三章 带刀老魁，背匣老黄].
long_form_mechanisms: Da Huang Ting (大黄庭) Energy Transmission: A supreme inner energy of the Wudang Sect. It requires lifelong cultivation. It can be transferred from a dying master to a recipient, but it requires the recipient's body to adapt and gradually unlock the energy's potential, as seen when Wang Chonglou transfers it to Xu Fengnian in [第三十一章 大黄庭].

Fujiang Hongjia (符将红甲) Puppet Creation: A legendary armor system made of special alloys/woods and driven by magic talismans and human hosts. Each armor represents one of the five elements (Earth, Water, Wood, Fire, Gold), and possesses near-indestructible defense and element-specific combat properties, as encountered in [第五十七章 大雨小道立红甲] and [第九十四章 死战].

One Sleeve of Green Snake (一袖青蛇) Sword Technique: Li Chungang's signature sword technique, which channels sharp, snake-like sword qi through the sleeve to strike the enemy with overwhelming force, capable of cutting through iron armor and separating rivers, cited in [第九十四章 死战] and [第一百三十六章 一袖如何两青蛇].

Confucian Sage (儒圣) Ascension: A unique path to the supreme martial realm where a scholar who does not practice physical martial arts achieves sudden ascension through complete understanding of principles, moral character, and reading, though it often comes at the cost of rapid life-force depletion, as demonstrated by Xuanyuan Jingcheng in [第一百八十二章 儒圣].

Reincarnation and Vows (洪洗象's Cultivation): The path of Wudang's patriarchs who undergo reincarnation (e.g. Lü Dongbin) and bind their power to specific vows (like 'not descending Wudang Mountain unless becoming the top under heaven'). Breaking the vow triggers the recovery of all past-life memories and powers, as shown in [第一百九十九章 仙人骑鹤下江南].

Yuan Shen Out-of-Body (元神出窍) and Rebirth: The ultimate state of Taoist cultivation where a master's spirit/soul can exit the physical body to ascend to heaven ('登仙') or survive the destruction of the physical shell, though the soul remains vulnerable to flying sword attacks and spiritual curses, as illustrated by Zhao Xuansu in [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].

Deng Tai'an's Flying Swords (桃花剑神飞剑): The mechanism of controlling twelve miniature swords (each with a specific name like Qingmei, Zhuque, Taia) using sword intent and mental control, capable of pinning down the physical gates/acupoints of even celestial beings, as described in [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].

Tingchao Pavilion's Manual Cataloging: A systematic collection of the world's martial arts books gathered by the Northern Liang army from defeated sects, structured across multiple floors, where higher floors contain increasingly secret and dangerous manuals, as described in [第二章 白狐儿脸] and [第六章 走一个].
continuity_observations: The 6000-mile Journey: The opening chapters frequently refer to the hardships and lessons learned during the three-year, 6000-mile travel of Xu Fengnian and Old Huang, which established their deep master-servant bond and Xu Fengnian's practical knowledge of the lower classes. Cited in [第一章 小二上酒] and [第十四章 劣马黄酒六千里].

Old Huang's Sword Box: Old Huang's wooden box containing his collected swords is a key item. Its origin, his loss of the first sword to Wang Xianzhi, and the subsequent retrieval of the box by Xu Fengnian form a core motivating thread. Cited in [第十三章 带刀老魁，背匣老黄] and [第二十章 杀人赏雪].

Jiang Ni's Dagger 'Shenfu' (神符): The short dagger 'Shenfu' was given to Jiang Ni by her royal parents before Western Chu fell. She keeps it hidden and uses it to repeatedly 'assassinate' or threaten Xu Fengnian, reinforcing her dual identity as his maid and enemy. Cited in [第三章 两个酒窝] and [第二十三章 小狗小泥人].

Wudang Mountain's Debt: Wudang Sect's decline in the shadow of Dragon Tiger Mountain's imperial favor drives Wang Chonglou's decision to sacrifice his life and transfer 'Da Huang Ting' to Xu Fengnian, ensuring Northern Liang's protection. Cited in [第三十一章 大黄庭] and [第三十二章 一肩挑道].

Li Chungang's Imprisonment: Li Chungang's presence in the carriage as a sheepskin-coat old man connects back to his secret imprisonment underneath Tingchao Pavilion by Xu Xiao after his historical defeat and broken heart. Cited in [第五十五章 一剑便是百万师] and [第八十二章 龙王爷一竿拦江].

Cao Changqing's Legacy: The arrival of Cao Changqing to take Jiang Ni away is set up by early references to his status as the 'Cao Guanzi' and the last grand scholar-general of Western Chu, who refused to accept the fall of his country. Cited in [第一百三十四章 曹官子] and [第一百三十六章 一袖如何两青蛇].

Hong Xixiang's Vow for Red Clothing: Hong Xixiang's refusal to descend the mountain and his waiting for 'the one in red' (Xu Zhihu) links back to their childhood encounters and Wudang's prophecy of his path. Cited in [第十五章 山上有个骑牛的] and [第一百九十章 等红衣].

Deng Tai'an's Connection to Northern Liang: Deng Tai'an's willingness to help Xu Fengnian and lend his swords links to his past debt to Xu Fengnian's mother, Wu Su, who was the previous owner of the sword Da Liang Longque. Cited in [第一百九十六章 壶酒双碗，端酒借剑一千九] and [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].
style_observations: Juxtaposition of High Fantasy and Mundane Realism: The author frequently contrasts grand, world-shaking martial arts (like Li Chungang's sword qi) with highly mundane, earthy details (like peeling sweet potatoes, eating wild fruits, or Old Huang's love for cheap yellow wine). Cited in [第一章 小二上酒] and [第十四章 劣马黄酒六千里].

Use of Abstract, Melancholic Poetry and Ballads: The narrative regularly embeds folk songs, poems, or historical laments (like '煌煌北凉镇灵歌' or Wudang's riddles) to create a tragic, elegiac tone for the fallen warriors and kingdoms. Cited in [第四十章 煌煌北凉镇灵歌] and [第一百七十三章 歌谣].

Indirect Characterization through Bystander Commentary: Key fights or displays of power are rarely described purely from the combatants' perspectives; instead, they are observed and analyzed by side characters (like Shu Xiu, Wei Shuyang, or random onlookers) who explain the stakes and technicalities. Cited in [第五十八章 水珠对水甲] and [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].

Cinematic Rain and Weather Symbolism: The author utilizes intense weather changes (sudden rainstorms, snowfalls, or thunderbolts) to mirror the emotional and combat escalation, such as the rainstorm during the Red Armor ambush or the lightning during Xuanyuan's death. Cited in [第五十七章 大雨小道立红甲] and [第一百八十一章 请老祖宗赴死].

Serial Novel Structural Clues (Chapter Cliffhangers): The chapters frequently end on dramatic proclamations or witty one-liners designed to keep the online reader engaged for the next day's update. Cited in [第二十五章 山下女子是老虎] and [第一百八十四章 还了个放屁].

Double Indentation and Typographical Compilations: The text maintains double full-width space indentation ('　　') at the start of each paragraph, with standard chapter heading formats ('第XX章 Title'), which reflects its origin as a compiled web novel text. Cited in [第一章 小二上酒] and [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].

creation_family_evidence.author: 烽火戏诸侯 (Fenghua Xizhuhou)
key_concepts: 一袖青蛇 (One Sleeve of Green Snake)
桃花剑神 (Peach Blossom Sword God)
creation_family_evidence.stylistic_signature: Combines epic, geopolitical wuxia with intimate, character-driven subplots. Features a melancholic focus on fallen kingdoms (Western Chu), heroic sacrifice (Old Huang, Wang Chonglou, Xuanyuan Jingcheng), and high-fantasy Taoist/Buddhist reincarnation systems (Hong Xixiang, Zhao Xuansu) integrated into a raw, historical-style wuxia world.
creation_family_evidence.compilation_indicators: The text features chapter titles formatted as '第XX章 Title' with double full-width space paragraph indentation. It contains characteristic web serial elements like inline author's notes (such as notes explaining character name pronunciations like '南宫仆射' in Chapter 5) and dramatic cliffhangers.

originality_risks: Direct Borrowing of Reincarnation and Lü Dongbin Legend: The character Hong Xixiang is explicitly written as the reincarnation of Lü Dongbin (the famous Taoist immortal from Chinese folklore) and his flying on a yellow crane ('骑鹤') directly borrows from the classic poem 'Yellow Crane Tower' (黄鹤楼) and standard Daoist mythology, rather than creating an original immortal lore. Cited in [第一百九十九章 仙人骑鹤下江南].

Duality of Wudang and Dragon Tiger Mountain: The geopolitical tension between Wudang (representing the underdog, pure Daoism supported by Northern Liang) and Dragon Tiger Mountain (representing the court-favored, political Daoism supported by the Imperial Palace) closely mirrors the classic wuxia division seen in Jin Yong's novels (where Wudang represents the orthodox, pure Sect, often in tension with other court-aligned forces). Cited in [第三十一章 大黄庭] and [第一百八十六章 四大天师].

The 'Underdog Scholar Sacrifices for Family' Trope (Xuanyuan Jingcheng): The narrative arc of a weak, humiliated scholar who silently tolerates decades of abuse only to suddenly reveal he has reached the ultimate realm and sacrifices himself to wipe out the corrupt ancestor is a highly standardized melodramatic trope in Chinese wuxia/xianxia literature. Cited in [第一百八十一章 请老祖宗赴死] and [第一百八十二章 儒圣].

The 'Disguised Child is a Secret Ancient Master' Trope: The character Zhao Xuansu disguising himself as a helpless child ('小虫子') to travel with the protagonist before attempting an assassination is a very common trope in classic wuxia novels (reminiscent of characters like Tianshan Tonglao in Jin Yong's Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils or similar characters in Gu Long's works). Cited in [第二百章 登仙？] and [第二百零一章 雷池和道理].

The 'Invincible, Arrogant Martial Emperor City' Concept: Wudi City, ruled by the undefeated Wang Xianzhi who sits at the top of the martial world and collects the weapons of defeated challengers on the city walls, draws clear inspiration from classic wuxia tropes like the 'Sword Tomb' (剑冢) or 'World's Best Pavilion' where challengers must leave their weapons upon defeat. Cited in [第二十章 杀人赏雪] and [第一百九十六章 壶酒双碗，端酒借剑一千九].
